newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-DENNIS RODMAN SAYS HE DIDN'T GROIN-KICK PHOTOGRAPHER.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-DENNIS RODMAN SAYS HE DIDN'T GROIN-KICK PHOTOGRAPHER.

text.p: Suspended Chicago Bulls forward Dennis Rodman denied Wednesday that he kicked a cameraman in the groin, saying it was a "tap" aimed at the man's camera.

The controversial five-time NBA rebounding king with multi-coloured hair and multiple tattoos said his reputation "is getting dragged all in quicksand, for no reason" and added that "I've done things that are very, very minor."

In a television interview taped in California, he said of the incident last week in Minneapolis: "If you look at my leg (you'll see) I'm kicking the camera. The camera went underneath his legs and my momentum, my leg hit his leg. It wasn't a groin. If you look at the tape it wasn't a groin ...
"If that's his groin ... my god, his wife must really love him."
He said the contact with cameraman Eugene Amos was no more than a "tap," adding that "I apologise for that but most of the people in the world would say he was acting."
Rodman was suspended for at least 11 games, fined $25,000 and ordered to see a counsellor because of the incident. The lost salary will cost him about $1 million.
He also has agreed to pay the cameraman $200,000 in an out-of-court settlement. He told the TV show he settled because didn't want to drag the matter out "like an O.J. Simpson trial."

Television pictures showed Rodman stumbling out of bounds, tripping over Amos, and then kicking him as he got up off the floor. Amos, in a delayed reaction, slumped over for more than five minutes before he was carried off and taken to a hospital.
It was just the latest in a series of incidents for Rodman and his second suspension of the season.

He earlier served a two-game team-imposed suspension for a profanity-laced tirade about the referees after a December 8 loss at Toronto. That suspension cost him $219,512, or 2/82nd of his 1996-97 salary of $9 million.
Last March he was suspended for six games after head-butting a referee at New Jersey.
Rodman helped Chicago post a record 72-10 mark last season and win the NBA championship, the Bulls' fourth in six years.
